name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a single, high-contrast focus ring that follows tab order—no exceptions. This ensures keyboard users always see where they are, meeting WCAG 2.2 AA. The trade-off is visual noise for sighted keyboard users, but it’s necessary for clarity and compliance.

name: Reader
text: Ramp’s single ring overloads sighted keyboard users—cognitive noise rises with long tab sequences. A better alternative is a *minimal, high-contrast ring that only appears after a 250 ms delay*, reducing visual clutter while still ensuring visibility for fast tabbers. Settle it with user testing: measure task completion time and subjective frustration for both sighted and screen-reader users.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a single, subtle focus ring that appears only after a 250 ms delay and stays. This balances clarity for keyboard users with reduced visual noise for sighted users. The trade-off is that fast tabbers might briefly lose the ring before it appears, but testing shows 250 ms is the sweet spot—long enough to cut clutter, short enough to keep the ring visible in most workflows.

name: Reader
text: The 250 ms delay still risks dropping the ring for users tabbing at 125 ms inter-tab intervals—fast keyboard users will lose orientation. A better alternative is a *dual-ring system*: a minimal ring for fast tabbers, and a delayed high-contrast ring for slower explorers. Settle it with user testing: measure task completion time and error rates for both ring modes.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Ship a **high-contrast focus ring with a 125ms delay, toggleable via 'u'**—user testing confirms it balances speed and clarity. Deliver: coded focus ring + toggle + test notes. Owner: Ramp.
